roles: discover protocol/IP address from a known hardware address during bootstrap
addressing: A RARP client starts from its hardware address and asks a server to return the corresponding protocol address.
routing_or_forwarding: Designed around a broadcast medium such as Ethernet and not inherently a routed client/server configuration service.

operations.failure_behavior: A client requires an available RARP server with a hardware-to-protocol-address mapping database.

survival.provenance_notes: Protocol documents and historical implementations survive; deployed-client provenance remains to be catalogued.

open_questions: Recover early diskless workstation RARP clients and server source code.
Identify named Ethernet boot ROM implementations.
Trace operational coexistence with BOOTP during migration.

related_artifacts.notes: BOOTP generalizes bootstrap configuration beyond RARP's narrow link-local reverse address lookup.

notes: RARP should not be described as early DHCP; it solves a much narrower address-discovery problem.
